chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn, from Murazim, from his brother who said:
A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A boy has been born to me.'
So he said: 'May Allah grant you thanking the Bestower, and bless you in the gift, and may he reach adulthood, and may Allah grant you his righteousness.'

key_terms.أشده: Ashuddahu — his full strength/maturity; referring to physical and intellectual adulthood, used in the Quran (e.g., 46:15)
key_terms.الموهوب: Al-mawhoub — the gift/endowment; refers to the newborn child as a blessing granted by God
key_terms.الواهب: Al-Wahib — The Bestower; one of the Names of Allah emphasizing His freely bestowing gifts without obligation
key_terms.بره: Birrahu — his righteousness/filial piety; the duty of children toward their parents

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic congratulation du'a for the birth of a child according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: A man informed Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) of the birth of his son, and the Imam responded with a traditional Islamic blessing encompassing gratitude to God for the gift of a child, blessings upon the child, prayers for the child to reach maturity, and for the father to benefit from the child's piety. This hadith establishes the Sunnah of congratulating those blessed with a newborn using a specific du'a that acknowledges God as the ultimate Giver (al-Wahib) while invoking His blessings on both the new father and the child.
